title: India Will Play Their First Test Series in Sri Lanka Since 2017. Here's What's at Stake.
excerpt: Two World Test Championship matches at Galle and Colombo in August mark India's return to the island after an eight-year gap — with their WTC final hopes hanging in the balance.
body:
India have not played a Test match in Sri Lanka since 2017, when Virat Kohli's side swept a three-match series 3-0 on spinning tracks that turned from Day 1. Eight years later, Shubman Gill's team will return to the island for a two-match Test series in August that could define their World Test Championship campaign.

Sri Lanka Cricket announced the schedule this week: the first Test will be played at the iconic Galle International Cricket Stadium from August 15-19, followed by the second at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground in Colombo from August 23-27. Both matches start at 10:00 AM IST.

## The WTC Stakes Are Real

India's WTC 2025-27 cycle has been a turbulent one. After splitting a home series against England 2-2 and sweeping the West Indies, a clean sweep loss to South Africa at home in November set them back significantly. A one-off Test win over Afghanistan last month helped, but India still sit fifth on the WTC points table with a win percentage of 48.15 — well behind the leaders.


![Virat Kohli — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/Virat_Kohli_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)


Sri Lanka are sixth at 44.44 per cent, having split their three completed matches between one win and one defeat against Australia. They are currently being hammered by the West Indies in Antigua, having lost the first Test by an innings and 217 runs.

For India, a 2-0 sweep in Sri Lanka is close to essential. Dropping points in either match would make the path to the WTC final — already narrow after the South Africa debacle — almost impossibly steep.



> **"They are currently being hammered by the West Indies in Antigua, having lost the first Test by an innings and 217 runs."**


## Galle: The Spinner's Paradise

The Galle International Cricket Stadium has historically been the most spin-friendly Test venue in world cricket, and India, with their deep spinning resources, have traditionally thrived there. Ravindra Jadeja, Ravichandran Ashwin (now retired from Tests), and the next generation of Indian spinners have turned Galle into a fortress in previous tours.


![Shubman Gill — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/34/Shubman_Gill_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg)


But Sri Lanka's home advantage at Galle is well-documented. The pitch deteriorates sharply from Day 3 onwards, and Sri Lanka's own spinners — whatever the vintage — have always been dangerous on home soil. India's batting lineup will need to score quickly and heavily in the first innings to avoid being caught on crumbling surfaces.

## India's Red-Ball Reset

The series represents a broader reset for India's Test ambitions. The current WTC cycle has exposed vulnerabilities in India's red-ball setup that weren't visible during their white-ball dominance. The batting order, in particular, has struggled away from home, with the middle order yet to find a reliable anchor beyond Gill himself.

Shreyas Iyer's Test recall remains uncertain. Rishabh Pant's availability will be a key question. And the bowling attack, while potent on paper, needs match fitness after months of T20 and ODI cricket against England in July.


![Galle International Cricket Stadium — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8f/Sri_Lanka_vs_Pakistan_test_match.JPG)


Gill, who led India's Test resurgence with a double century in England last year, will carry the weight of captaincy into conditions that demand patience, application and tactical clarity — all of which have been tested by India's recent red-ball form.

## The Bigger Picture

After the Sri Lanka tour, India face a packed Test schedule in the lead-up to the WTC final in mid-2027. Every series from here is effectively a knockout stage. The margins are thin. The competition — Australia, South Africa, England — is relentless.

For Indian fans, particularly those in the NRI community, the Galle Test starting on August 15 — India's Independence Day — adds an emotional layer. Sri Lanka is one of the easiest international destinations for Indian passport holders, and Galle has long been a favourite stop for travelling fans from across the subcontinent.

The schedule gives India seven weeks from the end of the England ODI series on July 19 to prepare for conditions that couldn't be more different from English seam and bounce.

*Sources: Khel Now, Sportskeeda, ESPNcricinfo*
